1	## Chapters
2	
3	### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains
4	
5	**Tutorial:**
6	
7	1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
8	2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
9	3. “Select Lyn.”
10	4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
11	5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
12	6. “Select attack!”
13	7. “Select Lyn.”
14	8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
15	9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
16	10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
17	11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.
18	
19	**Agent notes:**
20	
21	_(none yet)_
22	
23	### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate
24	
25	**Tutorial:**
26	
27	1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
28	2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
29	3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
30	4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
31	5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
32	6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
33	7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
34	   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
35	8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
36	9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
37	10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
38	11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
39	12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!
40	
41	**Agent notes:**
42	
43	_(none yet)_
44	
45	### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits
46	
47	**Tutorial:**
48	
49	1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
50	2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
51	3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
52	4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
53	5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
54	6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
55	7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
56	8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
57	9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!
58	
59	**Agent notes:**
60	
61	_(none yet)_
62	
63	### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries
64	
65	**Tutorial:**
66	
67	1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
68	2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
69	3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
70	4. Please select Lyn.
71	5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
72	6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
73	7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
74	8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
75	9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
76	10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
77	11. Select Wil.
78	12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
79	13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
80	14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
81	15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
82	16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
83	17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
84	18. You can also check on the item screen.
85	19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
86	20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
87	21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
88	22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.
89	
90	**Agent notes:**
91	
92	_(none yet)_
93	
94	### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow
95	
96	**Tutorial:**
97	
98	1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
99	2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
100	3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
101	4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
102	5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
103	6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”
104	
105	**Agent notes:**
106	
107	_(none yet)_
108	
109	### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders
110	
111	**Tutorial:**
112	
113	1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
114	2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
115	3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
116	4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
117	5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”
118	
119	**Agent notes:**
120	
121	_(none yet)_
122	
123	### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride
124	
125	**Tutorial:**
126	
127	1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
128	2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
129	3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
130	4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
131	5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
132	6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
133	7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.
134	
135	**Agent notes:**
136	
137	_(none yet)_
138	
139	### Chapter 7 — Siblings Abroad
140	
141	**Tutorial:**
142	
143	1. Starting with this chapter, you’ll be able to use the preparations screen. On this screen, you can choose who will fight, equip different items, and arrange your formation, among other things. If you have no special preparations to make, simply press START. This starts the chapter with the same group you were using at the end of the last chapter.
144	2. The monk Lucius has joined your group. Monks are users of the magic of light. Those who wield magic are highly attuned to its flow, so they have a high magic resistance. Units with high magic resistances can reduce the damage caused by magical attacks. When magic users battle each other, they often find it hard to inflict damage. The light magic of monks is strong against the dark magic favored by shamans. Lucius should come in handy here. Let’s put his magic to the test. Have Lucius attack the shaman nearest him.
145	3. It’s time to see what Nils can do. The music played by bards allows your allies to move twice in the same turn. However, bards cannot engage in combat, so be careful not to expose them to danger.
146	4. Through the power of Nils’s music, Lucius can move again this turn. Bards gain experience by playing music. Use Nils’s powers often, and increase his skill.
147	5. When you fulfill certain conditions, side quests may make themselves apparent to you. Side quests allow you to learn things that aren’t part of the main story. You might meet tough new enemies or find new companions to travel with. However, side quests are very difficult, and once you begin one, you must see it through to its end. If you plan to challenge a side quest, I suggest you keep the save data from the previous mission. Not accepting side quests will not effect your ranking. If you’re in a hurry to pursue the main story, skip the side quests.
148	
149	**Agent notes:**
150	
151	_(none yet)_
152	
153	### Chapter 7x — The Black Shadow (gaiden)
154	
155	**Agent notes:**
156	
157	_(none yet)_

159	### Chapter 8 — Vortex of Strategy

412	  - Rescue + canto works: Sain/Florina can Rescue a fragile unit and canto back out of reach (count enemy Move + 1 to every tile next to the carrier).
413	  - **Attempt 1 abandoned as unwinnable on turn 11.** Wallace died on turn 7 at the bridge (swarmed by about 6 Black Fang plus the Sniper; he never came near us). From turn 7 a big wave came down the west side from the north: about 5 Myrmidons (L10 Steel sword Atk 15, L15 Slim sword Atk 12), 4+ Monks, then Knights. Unarmed Hector, used as a wall, went 32 -> 15 -> 5 in two enemy phases (the Monks' Shine hits his Res 3). Hawkeye's Killer axe BROKE on turn 10 (13 uses do NOT last), which left no damage dealer at all.
414	  - LESSONS for the next attempt:
415	    1. Weapons are the real problem. Hawkeye's Killer axe (13 uses) must be saved for Lloyd and emergencies. Do NOT let him counter-kill every Monk and Myrmidon. The Armory (south-east, across the river) is the only fix. Florina (flier) can reach it in about 2 turns from the start; funds are 6150G. Buy axes for Hawkeye and Hector, plus Vulneraries at the Vendor next door. Beware the Sniper (Silver bow, kills fliers) and the ballista near there on turns 1-3. The Sniper walks north to fight Wallace at the bridge, so the armory may be safer from about turn 3-4.
416	    2. Never use weaponless Hector as a wall against Monks.
417	    3. Monks come in pairs; kill them first (Lyn doubles them for about 24).
418	    4. The enemy wave that hits us on turns 7-10 is big. Have a defensive spot ready (for example the bottom-left corner), not an open field.
419	    5. DECOY TRICK: once unarmed, Hawkeye (51 HP, Def 14, Res 11) took only 0-2 per hit, and ALL the nearby enemies (about 9) crowded around him for turns while ignoring everyone else. An unarmed high-defence unit is a perfect decoy. Monks do 0 to him.
420	    6. Lloyd probably sits still. Plan to chip him at RANGE 2 (Wil's bow, Hand axes, Javelins from the Armory), where his sword can't counter.
421	  - Attempt 1 ended on turn 12: I moved the doomed Eliwood forward and he fell, giving a Game Over so the chapter could be restarted with everyone alive.
422	  - s13 attempt 2 notes:
423	    - A SECOND SNIPER (38 HP, Silver bow) guards the south-east houses/armory, near map tile (13,9) (counting from the bottom-left start screen; the river is column 10). It is hidden in fog until a unit is within about 3 tiles. On turn 1 Florina flew to the river at (10,9). It moved next to her, shot and MISSED; then it stays on the east bank around (11,8). The armory run by Florina is NOT safe while it lives. Ground units can't cross the river in the south. Abandoned the armory plan.
424	    - Sain's Steel sword is NOT usable (no Attack option), even though the item screen shows Atk 21. Sain, Florina and Matthew have no usable weapon.
425	    - The two Wyvern Riders start in the north-west (by the village) and strike on the turn-3 enemy phase. One went for Hawkeye (bait at (2,5)) and died to his counter. The other flew round to the far west and hit Eliwood in the corner (13 dmg). Hawkeye killed it on turn 4 (axe beats lance: 20x2, 100% hit).
426	    - Good defensive pocket: the bottom-left corner. Put lords and the 1-HP Florina at (0,8)/(0,9)/(1,8) and fill every adjacent tile with sturdier units.
427	    - Monks: 2 at the start plus 3 from the north-east (arriving turns 4-6). Lyn kills a 22-HP Monk exactly with 11x2. Hawkeye one-shots them. Monk magic has RANGE 2, so blocking adjacent tiles does NOT protect Eliwood from them.
428	    - **Attempt 2 LOST in the turn-8 enemy phase.** Sain died on turn 6 (two Monks). On turn 8 I left Lyn (13 HP) out at (1,5) after killing a Monk, with Eliwood at 8 HP in the corner, then skipped about 600 frames without screenshots. A lord died to the next wave coming from the north-west (Myrmidons arrive around turns 7-9 from the NW, not only from the north).
429	    - The real problem in both attempts: NO HEALING. Every chip on Eliwood or Lyn is permanent, and the enemy keeps coming in waves. A full-strength turtle in the corner bleeds out. Ideas for next time:
430	      a. Forts heal: (6,0) and (7,1) on the start screen (just north of the start, past the sand). Park hurt lords there between waves.
431	      b. Check the NW village (by the wyverns' start, top-left) with a lord: it may give a healing item.
432	      c. Keep Lyn and Eliwood above 18 HP or out of reach at ALL times. Never attack with them if it leaves them exposed afterwards. Use Hawkeye (Def 14, Res 10) as the only front-liner.
433	      d. Screenshot every ~300 frames of the enemy phase.
434	  - s13 attempt 3 (turns 1-8 went cleanly, lords never hit). Opening that works:
435	    - T1: only Eliwood uses Afa's Drops; everyone else waits. Florina must NOT go to the river.
436	    - T2: Lyn kills Monk A from (3,4) (11x2 = 22, exact). Wil shoots Monk B from range 2. Hawkeye moves to (2,5) next to Lyn.
437	    - T3: Hawkeye kills the wounded Monk; Lyn finishes the Mercenary (who attacked her). Then Hector RESCUES Lyn (Aid 12, Con 5), and Florina rescues Eliwood and cantos to the corner (0,9), with Matthew at (1,9). Carried lords can't be targeted. The wyverns did not even come this time.
438	    - T4-T7: Hawkeye plus Wil kill the Mercenary and 4 Monks that trickle in from the north-east. Wil (15 HP) died to a Monk counter on t5. Don't let Wil trade with Monks at under 18 HP.
439	    - Sain always dies (no weapon, the Monks target him). Wallace ALWAYS dies on turn 7 at the north bridge; you can't save or recruit him from the west side.
440	    - (1,8) on the start screen cannot be stood on (Hector couldn't move there).
441	    - T8-T10: the NW wave (2 Myrmidons incl. a L15 Slim-sword one, 3+ Monks) came down past the forts at (5,2)/(6,3). Hawkeye fought them up there and his Killer axe BROKE on t10 again (about 13 uses: roughly 9 player-phase attacks plus a few counters). After that we have NO real damage dealer: Lyn alone (Mani Katti) can only kill Monks.
442	    - T11: Florina tried the Armory run (flew to the river at about (9,8)). SNIPER #2 is STILL by the river/armory on t11 (it never leaves to fight Wallace) and one-shot her (Florina: "I'm always such trouble"). The armory is unreachable by air while that Sniper lives, and we have nothing that can kill a 36-38 HP Sniper at range.
443	    - VERDICT after 3 attempts: with this roster (only Hawkeye's 13-use Killer axe and Lyn's Mani Katti as real weapons, no healer, no shop access) the chapter looks UNWINNABLE by brute force. Lloyd was never even reached or seen. Ideas the next session should try that I did NOT test:
444	      1. Check Pick Units / the convoy in Prep more carefully, and use Prep "Trade" to give Matthew or Hector anything usable.
445	      2. Visit the NW village (top-left, near the wyverns' start) and the houses near the forts with Lyn or Matthew; they may give a weapon or a Vulnerary.
446	      3. Rush Lloyd: the castle/gate at the top-left of the map (seen in the intro pan) is probably Lloyd's seat. Let Hawkeye's axe go ONLY into Lloyd (the Killer axe crits 52%, 25+ damage): carry the lords, avoid every fight, and walk straight north along the west edge from turn 1.
447	      4. Matthew has a Lockpick/Door key? Check the chests in the castle for weapons.
448	    - Attempt 4 discovery: FLORINA CARRIES A TORCH (2 uses). Item > Torch > Use lights up the fog around her. On t2 she flew to the far north-west (about 7 tiles north of the start, by the NW village) and used it. That revealed only the village, a house and 2 Mercenaries near the forts. LLOYD IS FURTHER NORTH than that, past the forts and the mountains: the map continues north for at least another screen.
449	    - BEST PLAN I can see: a Lloyd rush. Keep Hawkeye at full HP and do NOT spend a single Killer-axe use before Lloyd (it crits about 50%; a crit is about 75 damage). Carry the lords (Hector carries Lyn, Florina carries Eliwood), walk north along the west edge, and dodge the waves instead of fighting them. Have Lyn kill only Monks that block the way. Check Lloyd's stats with R the moment he is visible.
450	    - **Attempt 3 LOST on the turn-12 enemy phase.** Lyn was swarmed by about 8 enemies after killing a Monk at (5,5), and her MANI KATTI BROKE. It starts this chapter with only about 10 uses! So the army's total offence for the whole chapter is about 13 Killer-axe uses plus about 10 Mani Katti uses plus Wil's Steel bow. Every attack has to count.

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow

**Tutorial:**

1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders

**Tutorial:**

1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride

**Tutorial:**

1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 7 — Siblings Abroad

**Tutorial:**

1. Starting with this chapter, you’ll be able to use the preparations screen. On this screen, you can choose who will fight, equip different items, and arrange your formation, among other things. If you have no special preparations to make, simply press START. This starts the chapter with the same group you were using at the end of the last chapter.
2. The monk Lucius has joined your group. Monks are users of the magic of light. Those who wield magic are highly attuned to its flow, so they have a high magic resistance. Units with high magic resistances can reduce the damage caused by magical attacks. When magic users battle each other, they often find it hard to inflict damage. The light magic of monks is strong against the dark magic favored by shamans. Lucius should come in handy here. Let’s put his magic to the test. Have Lucius attack the shaman nearest him.
3. It’s time to see what Nils can do. The music played by bards allows your allies to move twice in the same turn. However, bards cannot engage in combat, so be careful not to expose them to danger.
4. Through the power of Nils’s music, Lucius can move again this turn. Bards gain experience by playing music. Use Nils’s powers often, and increase his skill.
5. When you fulfill certain conditions, side quests may make themselves apparent to you. Side quests allow you to learn things that aren’t part of the main story. You might meet tough new enemies or find new companions to travel with. However, side quests are very difficult, and once you begin one, you must see it through to its end. If you plan to challenge a side quest, I suggest you keep the save data from the previous mission. Not accepting side quests will not effect your ranking. If you’re in a hurry to pursue the main story, skip the side quests.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 7x — The Black Shadow (gaiden)

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 8 — Vortex of Strategy

**Tutorial:**

1. On the far side of the hill to the south is a ballista. As Kent said, it’s a weapon intended for trained archers. The attack range of ballistae is extremely large, so they can fire on enemies at great distance. As they can attack without fear of counterattack, they’re quite useful. To use one, move an archer onto an unoccupied ballista, and select the ride command. After that, you can attack as usual. Ballistae can also be moved while in use. Additionally, ballistae can be used by any archer in the field. So, if you can remove the enemy manning the ballista and move one of your group onto it… you’ll find it most useful.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 9 — A Grim Reunion

**Tutorial:**

1. Wallace is a level 12 knight. He can rise as high as level 20. Most units can change classes once they reach level 10. By changing classes, units can improve all of their abilities. Movement range, constitution, usable weapons… Everything. There are many benefits. With a single action, you can make your units significantly more powerful. In order to change classes, units need to be of a certain level. However, you also need a special item. For example, Wallace is carrying a knight crest. With this, cavaliers and knights can change classes. Each character class has its own unique item that allows units of that class to switch to a different class. Well then, why don’t we try changing class now? Select Wallace, then choose knight crest from his items and use it.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 10 — The Distant Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Here ends Lyn’s story. Would you like to save your progress? [Yes] [No]  
   Would you like to continue playing? [Yes] [No]
2. As of Chapter 11, Eliwood becomes the story’s main character. Mark’s role will be to act as tactician, aiding his group. Help Eliwood to fulfill the chapter goals and fight his way to the end of the game. You’ll start your first campaign with Eliwood, then meet his friend, Hector, in chapter 12. And who knows? You might even meet Lyn again. If any of these three is defeated, your game will be over. The game will continue if any other allied units are defeated. However, a defeated unit can never take part in combat again, so be careful!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

## Hector mode

### Chapter 11 — Another Journey

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 12 — Birds of a Feather

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 13 — In Search of Truth

    - T4-T7: Hawkeye plus Wil kill the Mercenary and 4 Monks that trickle in from the north-east. Wil (15 HP) died to a Monk counter on t5. Don't let Wil trade with Monks at under 18 HP.

On t2 she flew to the far north-west (about 7 tiles north of the start, by the NW village) and used it. That revealed only the village, a house and 2 Mercenaries near the forts. LLOYD IS FURTHER NORTH than that, past the forts and the mountains: the map continues north for at least another screen.

Carry the lords (Hector carries Lyn, Florina carries Eliwood), walk north along the west edge, and dodge the waves instead of fighting them. Have Lyn kill only Monks that block the way. Check Lloyd's stats with R the moment he is visible.

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow

**Tutorial:**

1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders

**Tutorial:**

1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride

**Tutorial:**

1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 7 — Siblings Abroad

**Tutorial:**

1. Starting with this chapter, you’ll be able to use the preparations screen. On this screen, you can choose who will fight, equip different items, and arrange your formation, among other things. If you have no special preparations to make, simply press START. This starts the chapter with the same group you were using at the end of the last chapter.
2. The monk Lucius has joined your group. Monks are users of the magic of light. Those who wield magic are highly attuned to its flow, so they have a high magic resistance. Units with high magic resistances can reduce the damage caused by magical attacks. When magic users battle each other, they often find it hard to inflict damage. The light magic of monks is strong against the dark magic favored by shamans. Lucius should come in handy here. Let’s put his magic to the test. Have Lucius attack the shaman nearest him.
3. It’s time to see what Nils can do. The music played by bards allows your allies to move twice in the same turn. However, bards cannot engage in combat, so be careful not to expose them to danger.
4. Through the power of Nils’s music, Lucius can move again this turn. Bards gain experience by playing music. Use Nils’s powers often, and increase his skill.
5. When you fulfill certain conditions, side quests may make themselves apparent to you. Side quests allow you to learn things that aren’t part of the main story. You might meet tough new enemies or find new companions to travel with. However, side quests are very difficult, and once you begin one, you must see it through to its end. If you plan to challenge a side quest, I suggest you keep the save data from the previous mission. Not accepting side quests will not effect your ranking. If you’re in a hurry to pursue the main story, skip the side quests.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 7x — The Black Shadow (gaiden)

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 8 — Vortex of Strategy

**Tutorial:**

1. On the far side of the hill to the south is a ballista. As Kent said, it’s a weapon intended for trained archers. The attack range of ballistae is extremely large, so they can fire on enemies at great distance. As they can attack without fear of counterattack, they’re quite useful. To use one, move an archer onto an unoccupied ballista, and select the ride command. After that, you can attack as usual. Ballistae can also be moved while in use. Additionally, ballistae can be used by any archer in the field. So, if you can remove the enemy manning the ballista and move one of your group onto it… you’ll find it most useful.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

+      - Sain carrying Lyn (Spd halved, so doubled) died on the t2 EP to one Monk plus one Mercenary. Weak carriers die. Only HAWKEYE (Def 14, Res 10, 50 HP; Aid 15 so he can carry Eliwood or Lyn) and HECTOR (Def 13; Aid 12) are safe carriers.
